itens.t: James Webb Space Telescope captures turbulent star nursery in stunning new image

The James Webb Space Telescope captured a detailed image of a turbulent star-forming region named N159. Located 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud, the area is filled with dense clumps of gas.

Astronomers note that this region features a lower metallicity than the Milky Way. This characteristic allows scientists to study conditions similar to those found in the early universe and learn more about how stars formed.
